questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 ?
questions.explain: Count the 2s: there are 4 of them, so this is 4 groups of 2, which is 4 × 2 = 8. Counting one group too many gives 5 × 2, which is 2 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 2 × 2 or 5 × 4. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Xin Yi works out 3072 + 4353 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Xin Yi works out 3072 + 4353 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 12 is the tens column: 7 + 5 = 12, and no other column reaches ten. 12 tens is 1 hundred and 2 tens, so the 2 stays in the tens column - worth 20 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The small 1 is worth 100. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: PQRS is a trapezium in which the side PQ is parallel to the side SR. The side PS and the side QR each join the two parallel sides. ∠P = 59° and ∠Q = 107°. How many degrees larger is ∠S than ∠R?
questions.explain: ∠P and ∠S are at the ends of PS, which crosses the parallel pair, so ∠S = 180° − 59° = 121°. The same for QR: ∠R = 180° − 107° = 73°. The difference is 121° − 73° = 48°.
